topline.text: Quiet 24 hours nationally - the one notable move is a leadership change at the top of the DfE, not a policy announcement.
Simon Ridley has been appointed the department's new Permanent Secretary, replacing Susan Acland-Hood, who is leaving for a role outside government.
Today is the last working day before Sheffield schools break for autumn half term (26-30 October).

diary.text: South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority Board meets.
NEU's formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload closes.

items.lede: New Permanent Secretary named at the Department for Education.
items.body: Simon Ridley - currently Second Permanent Secretary at the Home Office - has been appointed the DfE's new top civil servant, succeeding Susan Acland-Hood. Education Secretary Lucy Powell welcomed the appointment; it's an administrative change rather than a policy shift, but worth knowing given how much DfE direction runs through this role.

box.label: Jargon-buster - Permanent Secretary
box.intro: Today's top story is about the DfE's new Permanent Secretary - a role that shapes education policy long after ministers move on.
box.text: The Permanent Secretary is the most senior civil servant in a government department, running it day-to-day and advising ministers. Unlike the Education Secretary (currently Lucy Powell), a political appointee, the Permanent Secretary stays in post across changes of government and minister.
